subject: Startups
title: When Regulations Kill Startups
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: When Regulations Kill Startups.

hook.text: Theranos promised to revolutionize blood testing. Regulatory fraud—not bad tech—is what sent Elizabeth Holmes to prison.

buildup.text: Regulated industries—healthcare, finance, education—have compliance requirements that can double development timelines.

discovery.text: GDPR in Europe imposed massive fines for data violations.

twist.text: Regulation creates moats too. Once you're compliant, the barrier to entry keeps underfunded competitors out.

climax.text: The smartest startups in regulated industries hire compliance experts early, not after the first audit.

punchline.text: Regulation is a cost and a moat. Play it right.

quiz.question: How can regulations benefit established startups?
options: Compliance creates barriers that keep competitors out
They eliminate the need for lawyers
